A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2. Their main text, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–G are readable and support matching content across substantial table reorganization and dataset substitutions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Section 5 and Appendices C–D, plus evaluations of LLM judges against human annotations in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and human-agreement results and adds comprehensive evaluations using LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework, classification judging, regression post-processing, N/A handling and relative-score aggregation remain unchanged. Appendix E's prompts are identical. Applying the existing pipeline with another evaluator changes the experimental condition rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Table 4 and Appendices C–D document substantial dataset substitutions: FluentSpeechCommands becomes SLURP, IEMOCAP becomes RAVDESS, VoxCeleb1 becomes the reconstructed SUPERB Hidden Set, and GTZAN-based evaluations are replaced or removed. Other replacements include CORAA with CommonVoice17, SBCSAE with CHIME6, and SceneFake with ASPIRE. The broad speech/music/audio scope and stated 180-task framing remain.

E2.justification: The nine evaluated model configurations and eight judges in the human-agreement study are retained. Qwen-Audio-Chat, Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct and GAMA-IT clarify names already appearing in v1's Figure 3; they do not establish new comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds a benchmark-wide evaluation condition using LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct alongside GPT-4o; v1 used open-source judges only in the small human-agreement study. Appendix C also adds LibriSpeech-TestOther evaluations for ASR, phoneme recognition and speaker verification, extending testing within the retained corpus.

E4.justification: The added alternative-judge results provide task-level evidence about evaluator sensitivity beyond the retained human-agreement study. However, v2 adds no dedicated analysis quantifying cross-judge agreement, controlled model ablations or systematic error study.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix E retains the same 150-example classification and regression validation sets and reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces important findings under changed datasets: WavLLM's emotion accuracy is 79.1% on IEMOCAP in v1 and 12.1% on RAVDESS in v2; SALMONN-13B's speaker-verification accuracy is 93.5% on VoxCeleb1 versus 51.0% on the SUPERB Hidden Set. These are not same-setting performance declines. Appendix C adds extensive LLaMA-judged results and revises retained entries, while Figure 11 changes the proportion exceeding 30 seconds from 7.11% to 6.57%.

T1.justification: The task formulation, evaluation definitions and relative-score calculation are retained. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace WavLLM with Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct as the emotion-recognition success example. The central contributions—a large collaborative benchmark, detailed taxonomy and evidence of limited model generality—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly warns that GPT-4o updates can affect reproducibility, attributes SALMONN's phoneme-recognition advantage to task-specific training, and explains why adapted HEAR/MARBLE results cannot be directly compared with their original benchmarks. The existing general limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit repository and dataset-license access instructions and clarifies model variants. Conversely, Table 4 replaces detailed HeteronymEn and Promo construction descriptions, including their synthesis sources, with 'self-constructed,' removing some reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Dataset recuration adds and removes references, including new SLURP, CHIME6, ISMIR04 and RemFx citations. The GAMA citation changes from Deshmukh et al.'s Audio Entailment paper to Ghosh et al.'s GAMA paper. The broader related-work positioning and novelty argument remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, standardizes task and model names, corrects inconsistent task-count wording, updates authors and publication headers, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Appendix C's four densely compressed result tables become substantially more readable multipage tables organized by evaluator, with dataset-qualified task labels. Table 4 is reordered and color-codes core benchmarks. Figures and several tables are resized or relocated, and Figure 11 is redrawn; the taxonomy graphics themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's unresolved licensing caveat and compressed tables, v2 documents replacement datasets and access information, improves result readability, and supplies a full open-source-evaluator reference. These changes improve reuse and auditability. The gain is tempered by unexplained score revisions, unexamined evaluator discrepancies and reduced construction detail for some synthetic datasets.
